description: Executable Candidate recipe of NVIDIA's DGX Spark playbook (vllm) for Llama 3.1 405B Instruct AWQ INT4: vllm 0.21.0+2325b6f0 (NVIDIA NGC vllm 26.05.post1-py3), pinned by arm64 digest, serving the exact model revision through `vllm serve` with the playbook's flags (vLLM defaults where the playbook passes none). Tensor parallel 2 across the pair uses vLLM's native multi-node launch (the platform's --nnodes/--node-rank placement options) instead of the playbook's hand-started Ray cluster: the pinned NVIDIA NGC vllm 26.05.post1 image does not ship Ray (its layers hold no ray package and no ray executable), and vLLM rejects --nnodes with the Ray executor. Deviation from the playbook: the context is 512 tokens (batched tokens 512) instead of 64, so the sweep's 256-token A323 chat case plus its prompt fits the context and the bounded 64-token chat check fits too. Resource envelopes budget the explicit GPU memory utilization plus unified-memory overhead, not measurements; physical Spark acceptance is pending. Memory follows the creator's settings: GPU memory utilization 0.9 with no explicit KV pool, the playbook's 405B launch at 98b3a473 (nvidia/vllm/README.md line 451; line 434 warns the 405B model has insufficient memory headroom for production use). The earlier 0.85 came from the 2026-10-11 offline memory fit (#1176) and the 1 GiB pool from the KV need check (#1946), not from a hardware run; the 0.85 content was OOM-killed at start on two Sparks on 2026-11-01, so this restore is the creator's value, not a fix for that failure. The declared peak is the admission maximum, an estimate until the run measures it.
title: Llama 3.1 405B Instruct AWQ INT4 vLLM two Sparks (NVIDIA playbook)
